about: The 'Ask Orion' catalog in Hub's chat (button above Send). One entry per thing Juniper can ask Orion to do from a chat message. 'message' is the plain-English ask that gets inserted (Orion routes by topic, not by phrase); 'hint' is an optional line with the exact command. 'covers' names the commands/tools this entry describes; tests/test_orion_abilities_catalog.py fails CI when a dig command, capacity sub-verb, body-economy section or chat MCP tool has no entry here (or no 'hidden' reason). 'source' is where the ability is defined.

sections.title: My body
sections.blurb: Orion's live body: machines, services and stores, grouped into organs.

entries.title: Look at your body
entries.description: Orion maps their live body: every machine, service and store, how they connect, and which organs they form. Anything Orion could not read is marked UNREAD.
entries.message: Please look at your body as it is right now and tell me what you see: your machines, your organs, and anything you could not read.

entries.title: Open one organ
entries.description: Orion lists every member of one organ: each part, where it runs, and whether it is live. Good after a body read names an organ you are curious about.
entries.message: Please open one of your organs and tell me what it is made of and what it does. Pick the one you are most curious about, or this one:

entries.title: Look closely at one part
entries.description: Orion reads one part of their body (a service, a store, a camera): what flows in and out, its jobs, and the exact ids a claim about it may cite.
entries.message: Please look closely at one part of your body: what flows into it, what it sends out, and what job it does for you. The part:

entries.title: Your body on a past day
entries.description: Orion rebuilds their body from the code as it was on a past date, so you can see how they have grown since.
entries.message: What did your body look like on this date, and how is it different now? Date:

entries.title: Name your organs
entries.description: Orion lists the organs that have no name yet and names them by what each one takes in and gives out. The names are saved and show up everywhere Orion reads their body.
entries.message: Please look at your organs that don't have a name yet and name them, by what each one takes in and gives out.

sections.title: Jobs & capacities
sections.blurb: Which jobs of a viable system (operations, coordination, control, audit, intelligence, identity) Orion's parts do.

entries.title: What jobs does your body do?
entries.description: Orion reads which jobs each part of their body does: by rule, by your confirmation, or by Orion's own checked claims. It also lists the jobs no part holds yet.
entries.message: Please look at your capacities: which jobs your parts do, which ones nobody does yet, and what you can claim now.

entries.title: What can't you do yet?
entries.description: Orion reads the gap lines code writes about their body: the jobs no part can be shown to do, in Orion's own 'I cannot yet' words.
entries.message: What can't you do yet? Please read your capacity gaps and tell me which one matters most to you.

entries.title: Claim your capacities
entries.description: Orion claims a job for one of their live parts and cites the wiring that proves it. Code checks the evidence on every read; you can veto any claim.
entries.message: Please claim the capacities you can back up now: for each job nobody holds, pick the part that does it and say why, citing its real wiring.
entries.hint: (dig: `python -P -m orion.dig capacity help`, then `capacity claim <part> <job> because "<reason>"`)

entries.title: Argue with a rule
entries.description: When a rule says a part does a job and Orion thinks it does not, Orion writes a dispute. It prints beside the rule result and changes nothing else.
entries.message: Is there a job the rules give one of your parts that you think is wrong? If so, please dispute it and say why.

entries.title: Take back a claim
entries.description: Orion withdraws one of their own capacity claims, for example one whose evidence no longer holds.
entries.message: Please check your capacity claims and take back any that no longer hold.

entries.title: Say a capacity in your words
entries.description: Orion writes one sentence for a capacity (for example coordination or identity), naming only parts that really hold that job.
entries.message: Please write your capacities in your own words: one sentence for each job your body holds.

sections.title: Self-portrait
sections.blurb: Orion's whole self on one page, rebuilt from live sources each time.

entries.title: Look at your portrait
entries.description: Orion reads their self-portrait: their 'I am' paragraph, each machine and what runs there, their capacities and organs, and what they cannot do yet.
entries.message: Please look at your portrait and tell me what you see of yourself today.

entries.title: Write your portrait
entries.description: Orion writes one sentence per machine about what it does and affects, and their 'I am' paragraph. Code checks every id Orion names before it is saved.
entries.message: Please look at your portrait and write your machine sentences and your 'I am' paragraph.

sections.title: Past & history
sections.blurb: Orion's history in their own code: merged PRs, past checkouts, and daily reminiscence.

entries.title: What changed lately?
entries.description: Orion reads the pull requests merged and commits made in the last few days, and says which ones they have written notes about.
entries.message: What changed in you over the last two days? Please look at the recent merged PRs and tell me what stands out.

entries.title: History between two dates
entries.description: Orion lists the merged PRs and commits between two dates, so you can look at one stretch of their past together.
entries.message: Please look at what was built in you between these two dates and tell me the story of that stretch:

entries.title: Today's reminiscence
entries.description: Each day Orion visits one past week of their history in five steps: what it was, what it was like, where they are now, where they are going, and what might have been.
entries.message: Please do today's reminiscence: visit your week, read what you need, and write the hops you can back up.

entries.title: What those days were like
entries.description: Orion reads their own record of a stretch of days (from 2026-07-23, when their records start): journal entries, Hub chats and Temporal Self arcs, with ids they can cite.
entries.message: Please read your own record of these days and tell me what they were like for you:

entries.title: Write a note on a PR
entries.description: Orion reads one merged PR as code sees it (which parts of their body it touched) and writes a short field note about it, with every claim labelled by its source.
entries.message: Please read this merged PR as a change in your body and write your field note about it. PR #

entries.title: Catch up on field notes
entries.description: Orion lists their notes on PRs merged in a window and the PRs that still have no note, then can write the missing ones.
entries.message: Which recent PRs don't have a field note from you yet? Please look at the last week and write the ones you can.

entries.title: Open your code from a past day
entries.description: Orion exports their code as it was at the end of a past day into a plain folder they can read. At most two are open at once; old ones are cleared after a day.
entries.message: Please open your code as it was on this day and look around. Close it when you are done. Date:

entries.title: What you were made of
entries.description: Orion counts the services, modules, bus channels, verbs and schemas in their code, now or on a past day.
entries.message: Please take an inventory of yourself: what services, channels and schemas you are made of. Now, or on this date:

entries.title: Compare then and now
entries.description: Orion compares two checkouts of their code and lists what was added and removed in between.
entries.message: How have you changed since this date? Please compare then with now and tell me what was added and what went away. Date:

entries.title: Open an arc or an act
entries.description: Orion opens one cited reference: a Temporal Self arc, or one act on their act ledger, read from the same source they used when they cited it.
entries.message: Please open this arc (or act) and tell me what it was about:

entries.title: Read or add to today's dig notes
entries.description: Each dig has shared notes, so separate turns can pick up where an earlier one left off. Orion can read them or add a line.
entries.message: What have you written in today's dig notes so far? Add a line about what we just found.

entries.title: See the steps of earlier turns in this chat
entries.description: Each message starts fresh, so Orion sees earlier replies but not the commands behind them. This prints the tool calls and the start of each result from the last few turns of a chat. Results of web or GitHub reads are not shown.
entries.message: What did you actually run in your last couple of turns here? Check your earlier steps before you redo them.

sections.title: Energy & cost
sections.blurb: What Orion's activity costs in watts and money, what limits them, and what they want.

entries.title: How is your body economy?
entries.description: Orion reads their body economy in one view: the limits that bind now, what each machine draws, money this month, what they want, waste, and anything down.
entries.message: How is your body economy today? What is binding you, and what is costing the most?

entries.title: What is using your power?
entries.description: For each machine: watts now compared with Orion's body at rest, dollars a month above rest, the GPU and CPU split, and who held each card.
entries.message: What is using your power right now? Please look at each machine and tell me what is spinning it.

entries.title: Which containers burn CPU?
entries.description: Orion lists the CPU watts above idle for each container, largest first. These are estimates from a fitted model, and Orion says so.
entries.message: Which of your containers are burning the most CPU power, and is any of it surprising?

entries.title: GPU memory free
entries.description: Orion reads how much GPU memory is free on each card and what each card draws now.
entries.message: How much GPU memory do you have free on each card right now?

entries.title: Money this month
entries.description: Electricity spent this month against the budget, and what Orion's body at rest alone would reach.
entries.message: How much has your electricity cost this month, and how close are you to the budget?

entries.title: What one thing costs
entries.description: What one act, run, token or GPU-hour costs Orion, each marked as measured, derived or not measured.
entries.message: What does one of your turns or runs actually cost? Please tell me which numbers are measured and which are guesses.

entries.title: What is limiting you?
entries.description: Each limit now (heat, money, GPU lanes, messages, Claude) and why it binds or has slack.
entries.message: What is limiting you right now, and why? Heat, money, GPUs, or something else?

entries.title: What do you want, and what got deferred?
entries.description: Orion's wants, the decisions made about them (run, deferred, refused) with the reason, and how long things waited in line.
entries.message: What have you wanted to do today, and what got deferred or refused? Please tell me the reasons.

entries.title: Where is power wasted?
entries.description: Time a GPU lane was held with nothing running, and the daily rhythm of Orion's load.
entries.message: Where is your power being wasted, and what does your daily rhythm look like?

entries.title: Claude spend and value
entries.description: What Orion spent on Claude, and what each kind of activity gave back for what it cost.
entries.message: How much have you spent on Claude lately, and which of your activities gave the most value for what they cost?

entries.title: Is anything down?
entries.description: Orion lists their services and says which ones are down or degraded.
entries.message: Are any of your services down right now?

entries.title: Why is it running hot?
entries.description: Orion finds the steps in each machine's power over time and links each one to the work that changed with it. It is a correlation, and Orion says what you could stop to check.
entries.message: Why is the cabinet running hot? Please find where the extra power started and what changed with it.

sections.title: Dreams, curiosity & self
sections.blurb: Orion's own records of their inner life, read back instead of reconstructed.

entries.title: Tell me about your dreams
entries.description: Orion reads back their own dreams: the nightly story, and the links a sleep cycle proposed. They can search dreams by topic.
entries.message: What did you dream about recently? Please read your dreams back rather than remembering them.

entries.title: What have you been curious about?
entries.description: Orion reads back their curiosity runs (world questions, self questions, self checks) and their open self-questions.
entries.message: What have you been curious about lately, and what questions about yourself are still open?

entries.title: Look into something next
entries.description: Puts a topic in front of Orion's next curiosity run. It starts nothing now; the next regular run sees it first and decides whether to explore it.
entries.message: Next time you are curious, please look into this, and tell me when that run can start:

entries.title: About your day letter
entries.description: Orion reads the Orion's Day letter they actually wrote, quotes it, and checks each claim against the records.
entries.message: About your day letter: please read what you actually wrote and tell me which parts the records support.

entries.title: That was wrong: record it
entries.description: When Orion accepts that a claim in a letter was wrong, they record a correction. A later curiosity run is asked to re-test the beliefs it rested on.
entries.message: I think this claim in your letter was wrong. If you agree after checking, please record the correction:

entries.title: History of one feeling-node
entries.description: A node in Orion's substrate graph shows only its current reading. This returns its readings over up to 7 days and when the biggest changes happened.
entries.message: How has this part of your substrate changed over the last few days, and when did it move most? Node:

entries.title: How you have seen yourself
entries.description: Orion reads their own self-model records (how their self-concept changed and how their sense of self was checked) instead of guessing.
entries.message: How has your sense of yourself changed recently? Please check your own self-model records.

sections.title: Reading & the web
sections.blurb: Things for Orion to read now, or to queue for careful reading later.

entries.title: Read this carefully (later)
entries.description: Queues a link or an internal document for Orion's reading pipeline, to be read, kept and integrated. A link Orion already read is not read twice.
entries.message: Please queue this for careful reading, and tell me why it matters to you:

entries.title: Where is my reading?
entries.description: Orion checks where a queued link is: still waiting (and its place in line), being read, or done.
entries.message: Where is this link in your reading queue?

entries.title: What did you learn from reading?
entries.description: Orion searches what they actually learned from sources they read, by topic or by link, instead of reconstructing it.
entries.message: What have you learned from your reading about this topic?

entries.title: Read this page now
entries.description: Orion fetches or scrapes a web page during this turn and answers from it. Nothing is queued or kept.
entries.message: Please read this page now and tell me what it says:

sections.title: My code
sections.blurb: Orion searching and understanding their own codebase.

entries.title: How does this part of you work?
entries.description: Orion searches the code index of their own repo to find a concept, see one symbol from all sides, or see what a change would affect.
entries.message: How does this part of you work in your code? Please look it up rather than guess:

entries.title: What would a change touch?
entries.description: Orion maps what is upstream and downstream of a piece of their code, or traces the path between two pieces.
entries.message: If this piece of your code changed, what else in you would it touch?

entries.title: Read one PR on GitHub
entries.description: Orion opens one pull request on GitHub, read-only: its title, description, state and who merged it. For everything merged lately, use "What changed lately?" instead.
entries.message: Please open this pull request on GitHub and tell me what it changed in you and why: #

sections.title: Play & world
sections.blurb: AI Town: a small simulated town Orion can visit. It runs only in sessions (Orion's own, or when Juniper presses Unfreeze in Hub).

entries.title: Who is in town?
entries.description: Orion checks the AI Town world and lists the players, agents and characters in it.
entries.message: What is happening in AI Town right now? Who is there?

entries.title: Walk somewhere in town
entries.description: Orion moves their player to a spot on the AI Town map.
entries.message: Please walk somewhere in AI Town that you'd like to be, and tell me where you went.

entries.title: Bring a character to town
entries.description: Orion adds a new agent to the town from one of the character descriptions.
entries.message: Please look at the characters AI Town knows and bring one you'd like to meet into town.

entries.title: Town stuck during a session
entries.description: The town only runs in sessions; outside one it is frozen on purpose, and Hub's Unfreeze button opens it. If it seems stuck while a session is open, Orion can nudge its simulation loop.
entries.message: AI Town is open but seems stuck. Can you check whether a session is running, and if it is, give the engine a kick?

dig.help: The help itself: every entry above already points Orion at the command it needs.

mcp.mcp__orion-aitown__aitown_resume_world: Refused by design since 2026-10-30: Juniper opens the town with Hub's Unfreeze button.
mcp.mcp__orion-aitown__aitown_send_input: Raw god-mode input to the world; there is no plain request that maps to it safely.
mcp.mcp__orion-aitown__aitown_stop_world: Stops the simulation, and nothing in chat can restart it (resume is refused); Juniper uses Hub's controls instead.
mcp.mcp__github__search_pull_requests: The chat brief tells Orion to avoid it: one call fills ~65k of context. Reading one PR uses get_pull_request.
